pairs.evidence: tools/voice/shadowrunr_voice/engine.py:154 The sidecar only gives Kokoro the model's stock US-English lexicon, so a recurring show's invented names and handles (Malakor, phylactery, chat usernames) are said however espeak guesses each time, with no recorded ruling per series; the technique requires a pronunciation ledger, and the repo's own design digest asks for a `world_lexicon.json`, which `git ls-files` does not contain.

techniques.evidence: tools/voice/shadowrunr_voice/engine.py:154 Partly realized: plus.py turns a structured {emotion,intensity,pace} cue into explicit sentence and clause pauses, speed and pitch, and the cue never sits in the spoken text. The technique's pronunciation-ledger rule is not met, though: the only lexicon is the stock one (engine.py:273-274 and warm.py:724 pass it only when it exists), and nothing normalizes figures for speech.

tools/voice/shadowrunr_voice/plus.py:76 Rate is a per-line pace cue for live speech. There is no fixed duration slot or word floor to budget against, and the technique's 'elastic duration' exclusion applies.
tools/voice/shadowrunr_voice/sidecar.py:7 The sidecar receives finished line text plus a separate delivery cue. There is no beat-chain artifact here, and the cue cannot change the words.

pairs.registryProposal: spoken-delivery-direction assumes a scripted narration with structural turns. For live, one-line-at-a-time character speech, the pause hierarchy can only be keyed to emotion and sentence or clause boundaries, not to argument turns. The technique could name that live-host case.

It does no casting, script adaptation, tone profiling or rate budgeting: searching apps/stage/src/voice for wpm, pronunciation, bookend and voice_profile found nothing.

techniques.evidence: apps/stage/src/voice/captions.ts:1 Speech is directed upstream, in the daemon or sidecar. The stage plays and displays it, timing captions on real audio duration rather than a word count.
